A former signwriter, he founded Bond Corporation and expanded into brewing and television, including ownership of the Nine network. His sprawling business empire subsequently collapsed, following the acquisition-driven expansion that had made him prominent.

long_biography.plain_text:
Three unsuccessful challenges preceded Alan Bond’s America’s Cup breakthrough. The Australian businessman headed the syndicate that owned Australia II, whose victory in 1983 ended 132 years of American possession of the trophy. Ben Lexcen’s winged-keel design and a Perth-based crew formed the centre of the winning campaign.

Bond also helped establish Australia’s first private, not-for-profit university, despite never having attended university himself. His corporation and Harunori Takahashi’s EIE financed the Gold Coast project through a joint venture. Bond University opened in 1989 with courses spanning business, law, science and the humanities. Financial trouble at the founding companies threatened the institution’s early survival; the university eventually bought its campus and buildings.

Ben Lexcen’s winged-keel design and a Perth-based crew formed the centre of the winning campaign.

Bond also helped establish Australia’s first private, not-for-profit university, despite never having attended university himself. His corporation and Harunori Takahashi’s EIE financed the Gold Coast project through a joint venture. Bond University opened in 1989 with courses spanning business, law, science and the humanities. Financial trouble at the founding companies threatened the institution’s early survival; the university eventually bought its campus and buildings.
